name: OLED 128×64 0.96" (SSD1306, SPI)
description: 0.96" monochrome OLED, 128×64 pixels, Solomon Systech SSD1306 controller on 4-wire SPI (D0 = clock, D1 = MOSI, DC = data/command, CS = chip select, RES = reset), internal charge pump, on-board 3.3 V regulator so it runs from 3.3–5 V. Sold as: generic 0.96" 7-pin SPI SSD1306 128x64 OLED module (blue PCB, header GND VCC D0 D1 RES DC CS; HiLetgo, DIYmall, AZ-Delivery and others).
eli5: A small, sharp screen that shows text and pictures with glowing dots. It uses a fast 5-wire connection instead of 2.

pins.name: RES
pins.description: Reset, active low (pulse low at least 3 us at start-up)

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command: low = command, high = display data

buildNotes: Header order is GND, VCC, D0, D1, RES, DC, CS. D0 is the SPI clock and D1 is MOSI; they are not GPIO numbers.
Drive the signal pins with 3.3 V logic: the SSD1306 logic supply on the module is 3.3 V.
Pulse RES low (at least 3 us) before sending commands, and enable the charge pump (8Dh 14h) before display on (AFh).
Keep the SPI clock at or below 10 MHz (datasheet tcycle min 100 ns). The display is write-only, so no MISO wire.
Some 0.96" SPI modules ship with an SH1106 instead; an image shifted by 2 columns means SH1106.

driver.code:
# SSD1306 0.96" 128x64 OLED on 4-wire SPI (7-pin module: GND VCC D0 D1 RES DC CS), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Solomon Systech SSD1306 datasheet Rev 1.1:
#   8.1.3  4-wire SPI: SDIN (D1) is shifted in MSB first on each rising SCLK (D0) edge while CS# is low;
#          D/C# is sampled with the 8th bit: LOW = command byte, HIGH = GDDRAM data byte.
#   13-4   tcycle >= 100 ns, so SCLK must stay at or below 10 MHz (this driver uses 8 MHz).
#   8.9    power-on: RES# low for at least 3 us, then high, before sending commands; SEG/COM come on
#          about 100 ms after AFh.
#   App note: the internal charge pump must be enabled (8Dh 14h) before AFh (modules have no external VCC).
import framebuf
import time


class SSD1306_SPI(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, width, height, spi, dc, res, cs, baudrate=8000000):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.spi = spi
        self.dc = dc
        self.res = res
        self.cs = cs
        self.rate = min(baudrate, 10000000)   # datasheet tcycle min 100 ns
        self.pages = height // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages * width)
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        cs.init(cs.OUT, value=1)
        dc.init(dc.OUT, value=0)
        res.init(res.OUT, value=1)
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        res(0)                                # RES# low >= 3 us
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        res(1)
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        self.init_display()

    def _write(self, dc, buf):
        # Mode 0: SCLK idles low, data is latched on the rising edge.
        self.spi.init(baudrate=self.rate, polarity=0, phase=0)
        self.cs(1)
        self.dc(dc)
        self.cs(0)
        self.spi.write(buf)
        self.cs(1)

    def cmd(self, *b):
        self._write(0, bytes(b))

    def init_display(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)                         # display off
        self.cmd(0xD5, 0x80)                   # clock divide ratio / oscillator (reset value)
        self.cmd(0xA8, self.height - 1)        # multiplex ratio (63 for 64 rows)
        self.cmd(0xD3, 0x00)                   # display offset 0
        self.cmd(0x40)                         # display start line 0
        self.cmd(0x8D, 0x14)                   # enable internal charge pump
        self.cmd(0x20, 0x00)                   # horizontal addressing mode
        self.cmd(0xA1)                         # segment remap: column 127 -> SEG0
        self.cmd(0xC8)                         # COM scan COM[N-1] -> COM0
        self.cmd(0xDA, 0x02 if self.width > 2 * self.height else 0x12)  # COM pins (0x12 for 128x64)
        self.cmd(0x81, 0xCF)                   # contrast
        self.cmd(0xD9, 0xF1)                   # pre-charge 1/15 DCLK (charge pump)
        self.cmd(0xDB, 0x40)                   # VCOMH deselect level
        self.cmd(0xA4)                         # display follows RAM
        self.cmd(0xA6)                         # normal, not inverted
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self.cmd(0xAF)                         # display on
        time.sleep_ms(100)                     # tAF: SEG/COM on after 100 ms

    def poweroff(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)

    def poweron(self):
        self.cmd(0xAF)

    def contrast(self, value):
        self.cmd(0x81, value & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def show(self):
        self.cmd(0x21, 0, self.width - 1)      # column address range
        self.cmd(0x22, 0, self.pages - 1)      # page address range
        self._write(1, self.buffer)            # DC high: GDDRAM data

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from ssd1306_spi import SSD1306_SPI

spi = SPI(1, baudrate=8000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({D0}), mosi=Pin({D1}))
oled = SSD1306_SPI(128, 64, spi, dc=Pin({DC}), res=Pin({RES}), cs=Pin({CS}))
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('SPI OLED', 0, 0)
oled.text('128x64 ok', 0, 56)
oled.show()
print('OLED ready')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
